title.narrative: Provision of emergency integrated health and nutrition services to conflict-affected communities of Ouanda-Djallé, Ouadda and Sam-Ouandja areas in the Central Africa Republic.

description.narrative: International Medical Corps (IMC) is a US-registered independent affiliate organization of International Medical Corps UK (IMC UK), with which IMC UK shares the same name and charitable objectives and mission. IMC UK and IMC work together to deliver assistance programs in an accountable and effective manner in pursuit of their commonly held charitable objectives. IMC UK will engage IMC to implement its programmes in the field, with IMC UK oversight, according to the terms and conditions of the agreement that results from this proposal and the terms of the parties’ administrative service agreement. Together with IMC Croatia, IMC provides administrative and operational support to IMC UK and to the programmes on the ground, including but not limited to financial management, banking and cash management, procurement management/international procurements and logistics. To contribute to meeting significant health needs in Ouanda-Djallé, Ouadda and Sam-Ouandja areas, IMC proposes 6 -months action to provide lifesaving primary health care services integrated with basic mental health services, essential nutrition services with mimimum WASH services to conflict affected and isolated communities with the aim of reducing excess morbidity and mortality amongst the vulnerable communities. CHF funding is critical to enable a rapid emergency assistance to these communities for whom needs continue to surpass the MoH capacity. PHC service package support will include outpatient curative consultations to treat common morbidities mental health consultation routine EPI services, sexual and reproductive health services (ANC, assisted deliveries, PNC, BEmONC services, Clinical Management of Rape and Intimate Partner Violence survivors (CMR IPV) supply of essential drugs, consumables and medical equipment capacity building trough trainings and supportive supervision community surveillance of epidemic disease, support to referral mechanisms with the involvement of CHW network and support of health information management system. IMC proposes to set up OTP services in each health facility and one Stabilization center in Ouanda-Djallé HF where 01 Medical doctor will be assigned and dedicated to performing clinical follow-up of SAM children with medical complication as well as conduct caesarean section. To fill the staffing gap at the MoH level, IMC will hire qualified health care providers (02 medical doctors, nurses, midwives, nutrition assistants, etc.) to improve the technical capacity of the HF and the quality-of-service delivery. Direct beneficiaries will be identified according to their exposure to risks, regardless of their status, age, religious belief, and gender. beneficiaries will be selected based on those people/communities affected by limited access to essential basic services (health, food, safe water, etc). This action will be implemented by IMC as the principal recipient of the funding in complementarity with 01 local NGO subcontractor, named‘’ Mouvement des Volontaires Africains pour le Developpment (MVAD) which will take over community activity component (community-based epidemiological and nutrition surveillance activities and distribution of mosquito nets. MVAD will support Ouadda PHC and OTP services under the technical support and supervision of IMC team. MVAD will establish its base in Ouadda while IMC will set up its operational sub-base in Ouanda-Djallé and Sam-Ouandja to enable close smooth implementation and supervision of the project activities. The project lifetime is 7 months: the first month will be dedicated to recruit the project staff, perform the pre-award assessment of the local NGO sub-partner and sign the sub-agreement. Prospection will be conduted in the project sites by IMC and MVAD team to identify and proceed with the rental of offices/guesthouses in Ouanda-Djallé, Ouadda and Sam-Ouandja areas during the first month. Other project activity implementation will start from the 2nd month of the project
